278: #ifndef CONFIG_DISABLE_PTHREAD
279:   if ((atomic_read(&tcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_MASK) !=
280:       TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_PTHREAD)
281: #endif
282:     {
283:       /* Get the TCB of the parent task.  In this case, the calling task. */
284: 
285:       FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
286: 
287:       DEBUGASSERT(rtcb != NULL && rtcb->group != NULL);
288: 
289:       /* Save the PID of the parent tasks' task group in the child's task
290:        * group.  Copy the ID from the parent's task group structure to
291:        * child's task group.
292:        */
293: 
294:       tcb->group->tg_ppid = rtcb->group->tg_pid;
295: 
296: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_CHILD_STATUS
297:       /* Tasks can also suppress retention of their child status by applying
298:        * the SA_NOCLDWAIT flag with sigaction().
299:        */
300: 
301:       if ((atomic_read(&rtcb->group->tg_flags) & GROUP_FLAG_NOCLDWAIT) == 0)
302:         {
303:           FAR struct child_status_s *child;
304: 
305:           /* Make sure that there is not already a structure for this PID in
306:            * the parent TCB.  There should not be.
307:            */
308: 
309:           child = group_find_child(rtcb->group, tcb->pid);
310:           DEBUGASSERT(child == NULL);
311:           if (child == NULL)
312:             {
313:               /* Allocate a new status structure  */
314: 
315:               child = group_alloc_child();
316:             }
317: 
318:           /* Did we successfully find/allocate the child status structure? */
319: 
320:           DEBUGASSERT(child != NULL);
321:           if (child != NULL)
322:             {
323:               /* Yes.. Initialize the structure */
324: 
325:               child->ch_flags  = ttype;
326:               child->ch_pid    = tcb->pid;
327:               child->ch_status = 0;
328: 
329:               /* Add the entry into the group's list of children */
330: 
331:               group_add_child(rtcb->group, child);
332:             }
333:         }
334: 
335: #else /* CONFIG_SCHED_CHILD_STATUS */
336:       /* Child status is not retained.  Simply keep track of the number
337:        * child tasks created.
338:        */
339: 
340:       DEBUGASSERT(atomic_read(&rtcb->group->tg_nchildren) < UINT16_MAX);
341: 
342:       atomic_add_relaxed(&rtcb->group->tg_nchildren, 1);
343: 
344: #endif /* CONFIG_SCHED_CHILD_STATUS */
345:     }
346: }
347: #else
348: #  define nxtask_save_parent(tcb,ttype)
349: #endif

351: /****************************************************************************
352:  * Name: nxtask_dup_dspace
353:  *
354:  * Description:
355:  *   When a new task or thread is created from a PIC module, then that
356:  *   module (probably) intends the task or thread to execute in the same
357:  *   D-Space.  This function will duplicate the D-Space for that purpose.
358:  *
359:  * Input Parameters:
360:  *   tcb - The TCB of the new task.
361:  *
362:  * Returned Value:
363:  *   None
364:  *
365:  * Assumptions:
366:  *   The parent of the new task is the task at the head of the ready-to-run
367:  *   list.
368:  *
369:  ****************************************************************************/
370: 
371: #ifdef CONFIG_PIC
372: static inline void nxtask_dup_dspace(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb)
373: {
374:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
375:   if (rtcb->dspace != NULL)
376:     {
377:       /* Copy the D-Space structure reference and increment the reference
378:        * count on the memory.  The D-Space memory will persist until the
379:        * last thread exits (see nxsched_release_tcb()).
380:        */
381: 
382:       tcb->dspace = rtcb->dspace;
383:       tcb->dspace->crefs++;
384:     }
385: }
386: #else
387: #  define nxtask_dup_dspace(tcb)
388: #endif

390: /****************************************************************************
391:  * Name: nxthread_setup_scheduler
392:  *
393:  * Description:
394:  *   This functions initializes the common portions of the Task Control Block
395:  *   (TCB) in preparation for starting a new thread.
396:  *
397:  *   nxthread_setup_scheduler() is called from nxtask_setup_scheduler() and
398:  *   pthread_setup_scheduler().
399:  *
400:  * Input Parameters:
401:  *   tcb        - Address of the new task's TCB
402:  *   priority   - Priority of the new task
403:  *   start      - Thread startup routine
404:  *   entry      - Thread user entry point
405:  *   ttype      - Type of the new thread: task, pthread, or kernel thread
406:  *
407:  * Returned Value:
408:  *   OK on success; ERROR on failure.
409:  *
410:  *   This function can only failure is it is unable to assign a new, unique
411:  *   task ID to the TCB (errno is not set).
412:  *
413:  ****************************************************************************/
414: 
415: static int nxthread_setup_scheduler(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb, int priority,
416:                                     start_t start, CODE void *entry,
417:                                     int ttype)
418: {
419:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
420:   irqstate_t flags;
421:   int ret;
422: 
423:   /* Assign a unique task ID to the task. */
424: 
425:   ret = nxtask_assign_pid(tcb);
426:   if (ret == OK)
427:     {
428:       struct tls_info_s *info = tcb->stack_alloc_ptr;
429: 
430:       /* Save PID to TLS */
431: 
432:       info->tl_tid = tcb->pid;
433: 
434:       /* Save task priority and entry point in the TCB */
435: 
436:       tcb->sched_priority = priority;
437:       tcb->init_priority  = priority;
438: #ifdef CONFIG_PRIORITY_INHERITANCE
439:       tcb->base_priority  = (uint8_t)priority;
440: #endif
441:       tcb->start          = start;
442:       tcb->entry.main     = (main_t)entry;
443: 
444:       /* Save the thread type.  This setting will be needed in
445:        * up_initial_state() is called.
446:        */
447: 
448:       ttype              &= TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_MASK;
449:       atomic_and(&tcb->flags, ~TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_MASK);
450:       atomic_or(&tcb->flags, ttype);
451: 
452:       /* Set the appropriate scheduling policy in the TCB */
453: 
454:       atomic_and(&tcb->flags, ~TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK);
455: #if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0
456:       atomic_or(&tcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_SCHED_RR);
457:       tcb->timeslice      = MSEC2TICK(CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL);
458: #else
459:       atomic_or(&tcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_SCHED_FIFO);
460: #endif
461: 
462:       /* Save the task ID of the parent task in the TCB and allocate
463:        * a child status structure.
464:        */
465: 
466:       nxtask_save_parent(tcb, ttype);
467: 
468: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
469:       /* exec(), task_create(), and vfork() all inherit the affinity mask
470:        * from the parent thread.  This is the default for pthread_create()
471:        * as well but the affinity mask can be specified in the pthread
472:        * attributes as well.  pthread_create() will have to fix up the
473:        * affinity mask in this case.
474:        */
475: 
476:       nxtask_inherit_affinity(tcb);
477: #endif
478: 
479:       /* exec(), pthread_create(), task_create(), and vfork() all
480:        * inherit the signal mask of the parent thread.
481:        */
482: 
483:       tcb->sigprocmask = rtcb->sigprocmask;
484: 
485:       /* Initialize the task state.  It does not get a valid state
486:        * until it is activated.
487:        */
488: 
489:       tcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_INVALID;
490: 
491:       /* Clone the parent tasks D-Space (if it was running PIC).  This
492:        * must be done before calling up_initial_state() so that the
493:        * state setup will take the PIC address base into account.
494:        */
495: 
496:       nxtask_dup_dspace(tcb);
497: 
498:       /* Initialize the processor-specific portion of the TCB */
499: 
500:       up_initial_state(tcb);
501: 
502:       /* Add the task to the inactive task list */
503: 
504:       flags = enter_critical_section();
505:       dq_addfirst((FAR dq_entry_t *)tcb, list_inactivetasks());
506:       tcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_INACTIVE;
507:       leave_critical_section(flags);
508:     }
509: 
510:   return ret;
511: }

176: /****************************************************************************
177:  * Name: nxtask_init
178:  *
179:  * Description:
180:  *   This function initializes a Task Control Block (TCB) in preparation for
181:  *   starting a new thread.  It performs a subset of the functionality of
182:  *   task_create()
183:  *
184:  *   Unlike task_create():
185:  *     1. Allocate the TCB.  The pre-allocated TCB is passed in argv.
186:  *     2. Allocate the stack.  The pre-allocated stack is passed in argv.
187:  *     3. Activate the task. This must be done by calling nxtask_activate().
188:  *
189:  *   Certain fields of the pre-allocated TCB may be set to change the
190:  *   nature of the created task.  For example:
191:  *
192:  *     - Task type may be set in the TCB flags to create kernel thread
193:  *
194:  * Input Parameters:
195:  *   tcb        - Address of the new task's TCB
196:  *   name       - Name of the new task (not used)
197:  *   entry      - Application start point of the new task
198:  *   actions    - File action to be performed.
199:  *   attr       - Use attr set stacksize, stackaddr and priority.
200:  *   argv       - A pointer to an array of input parameters.  The array
201:  *                should be terminated with a NULL argv[] value. If no
202:  *                parameters are required, argv may be NULL.
203:  *
204:  * Returned Value:
205:  *   OK on success; negative error value on failure appropriately.  (See
206:  *   nxtask_setup_scheduler() for possible failure conditions).  On failure,
207:  *   the caller is responsible for freeing the stack memory and for calling
208:  *   nxsched_release_tcb() to free the TCB (which could be in most any
209:  *   state).
210:  *
211:  ****************************************************************************/
212: 
213: int nxtask_init(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb, const char *name, main_t entry,
214:                 FAR const posix_spawn_file_actions_t *actions,
215:                 FAR const posix_spawnattr_t *attr,
216:                 FAR char * const argv[], FAR char * const envp[])
217: {
218:   int ttype = atomic_read(&tcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_MASK;
219: #ifdef CONFIG_MM_TASK_HEAP
220:   size_t heapsize = attr->heapsize;
221: #else
222:   size_t heapsize = 0;
223: #endif
224:   int ret = OK;
225: 
226:   sched_trace_begin();
227: 
228: #ifndef CONFIG_DISABLE_PTHREAD
229:   /* Only tasks and kernel threads can be initialized in this way */
230: 
231:   DEBUGASSERT(tcb && ttype != TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_PTHREAD);
232: #endif
233: 
234: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_ADDRENV
235:   /* Kernel threads do not own any address environment */
236: 
237:   if (ttype == TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_TASK)
238:     {
239:       FAR struct task_group_s *group =
240:         (FAR struct task_group_s *)(tcb + 1);
241: 
242:       if (group->tg_addrenv_own == NULL)
243:         {
244:           FAR struct addrenv_s *addrenv = addrenv_allocate();
245:           if (addrenv == NULL)
246:             {
247:               ret = -ENOMEM;
248:             }
249:           else
250:             {
251:               addrenv_attach(tcb, addrenv);
252:             }
253:         }
254:     }
255: 
256: #endif
257: 
258:   if (ret == OK)
259:     {
260:       /* Create a new task group */
261: 
262:       ret = group_initialize(tcb, atomic_read(&tcb->flags), heapsize);
263:       if (ret >= 0)
264:         {
265: #ifndef CONFIG_DISABLE_PTHREAD
266:           /* Initialize the task join */
267: 
268:           nxtask_joininit(tcb);
269: #endif
270: 
271: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_NOPREEMPT_KERNEL
272:           if (ttype == TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_KERNEL)
273:             {
274:               /* Disable pre-emption for this task */
275: 
276:               tcb->lockcount = 1;
277:             }
278: #endif
279: 
280:           nxsem_init(&tcb->exit_sem, 0, 0);
281: 
282:           ret = task_setup(tcb, name, entry, actions, attr, argv,
283:                            envp, ttype);
284:           if (ret >= 0)
285:             {
286:               /* Now we have enough in place that we can join the group */
287: 
288:               group_postinitialize(tcb);
289:             }
290:           else
291:             {
292:               nxtask_joindestroy(tcb);
293: 
294:               nxsem_destroy(&tcb->exit_sem);
295: 
296:               group_leave(tcb);
297: 
298: #ifdef CONFIG_ARCH_ADDRENV
299:               addrenv_drop(tcb->group->tg_addrenv_own, false);
300: #endif
301:             }
302:         }
303:     }
304: 
305:   sched_trace_end();
306:   return ret;
307: }
308: 
309: /****************************************************************************
310:  * Name: nxtask_uninit
311:  *
312:  * Description:
313:  *   Undo all operations on a TCB performed by task_init() and release the
314:  *   TCB by calling kmm_free().  This is intended primarily to support
315:  *   error recovery operations after a successful call to task_init()
316:  *   when a subsequent call to task_activate fails.
317:  *
318:  *   Caution:  Freeing of the TCB itself might be an unexpected side-effect.
319:  *
320:  * Input Parameters:
321:  *   tcb - Address of the TCB initialized by task_init()
322:  *
323:  * Returned Value:
324:  *   OK on success; negative error value on failure appropriately.
325:  *
326:  ****************************************************************************/
327: 
328: void nxtask_uninit(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb)
329: {
330:   irqstate_t flags;
331: 
332:   /* The TCB was added to the inactive task list by
333:    * nxtask_setup_scheduler().
334:    */
335: 
336:   flags = enter_critical_section();
337:   dq_rem((FAR dq_entry_t *)tcb, list_inactivetasks());
338:   leave_critical_section(flags);
339: 
340:   /* Release all resources associated with the TCB... Including the TCB
341:    * itself.
342:    */
343: 
344:   nxsched_release_tcb(tcb, atomic_read(&tcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_MASK);
345: }

47: /****************************************************************************
48:  * Name: nxtask_activate
49:  *
50:  * Description:
51:  *   This function activates tasks initialized by nxtask_setup_scheduler().
52:  *   Without activation, a task is ineligible for execution by the
53:  *   scheduler.
54:  *
55:  * Input Parameters:
56:  *   tcb - The TCB for the task for the task (same as the nxtask_init
57:  *         argument).
58:  *
59:  * Returned Value:
60:  *   None
61:  *
62:  ****************************************************************************/
63: 
64: void nxtask_activate(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb)
65: {
66:   irqstate_t flags = enter_critical_section();
67:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
68: 
69: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_INSTRUMENTATION
70: 
71:   /* Check if this is really a re-start */
72: 
73:   if (tcb->task_state != TSTATE_TASK_INACTIVE)
74:     {
75:       /* Inform the instrumentation layer that the task
76:        * has stopped
77:        */
78: 
79:       sched_note_stop(tcb);
80:     }
81: 
82:   /* Inform the instrumentation layer that the task
83:    * has started
84:    */
85: 
86:   sched_note_start(tcb);
87: #endif
88: 
89: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_PERF_EVENTS
90:   perf_event_task_init(tcb);
91: #endif
92: 
93:   /* Remove the task from waitting list */
94: 
95:   nxsched_remove_blocked(tcb);
96: 
97:   sinfo("%s pid=%d,TCB=%p\n", get_task_name(tcb),
98:         tcb->pid, tcb);
99: 
100:   /* Add the task to ready-to-run task list, and
101:    * perform the context switch if one is needed
102:    */
103: 
104:   if (nxsched_add_readytorun(tcb))
105:     {
106:       nxsched_switch(this_task(), rtcb);
107:     }
108: 
109:   leave_critical_section(flags);
110: }

104:    * type wrapped by pthread_addr_t is unknown.

123: static void pthread_start(void)

134:    * execution priority.

42: /****************************************************************************
43:  * Name: nxsched_set_affinity
44:  *
45:  * Description:
46:  *   sched_setaffinity() sets the CPU affinity mask of the thread whose ID
47:  *   is pid to the value specified by mask.  If pid is zero, then the
48:  *   calling thread is used.  The argument cpusetsize is the length (i
49:  *   bytes) of the data pointed to by mask.  Normally this argument would
50:  *   be specified as sizeof(cpu_set_t).
51:  *
52:  *   If the thread specified by pid is not currently running on one of the
53:  *   CPUs specified in mask, then that thread is migrated to one of the
54:  *   CPUs specified in mask.
55:  *
56:  *   nxsched_set_affinity() is identical to the function sched_setparam(),
57:  *   differing only in its return value:  This function does not modify
58:  *   the errno variable.  This is a non-standard, internal OS function and
59:  *   is not intended for use by application logic.  Applications should
60:  *   use the standard sched_setparam().
61:  *
62:  * Input Parameters:
63:  *   pid        - The ID of thread whose affinity set will be modified.
64:  *   cpusetsize - Size of mask.  MUST be sizeofcpu_set_t().
65:  *   mask       - The location to return the thread's new affinity set.
66:  *
67:  * Returned Value:
68:  *   Zero (OK) if successful.  Otherwise, a negated errno value is returned:
69:  *
70:  *     ESRCH  The task whose ID is pid could not be found.
71:  *
72:  ****************************************************************************/
73: 
74: int nxsched_set_affinity(pid_t pid, size_t cpusetsize,
75:                          FAR const cpu_set_t *mask)
76: {
77:   FAR struct tcb_s *tcb;
78:   irqstate_t flags;
79:   int ret = OK;
80: 
81:   DEBUGASSERT(cpusetsize == sizeof(cpu_set_t) && mask != NULL);
82: 
83:   /* Make sure that affinity mask is valid */
84: 
85:   if (*mask == 0)
86:     {
87:       return -EINVAL;
88:     }
89: 
90:   /* Verify that the PID corresponds to a real task */
91: 
92:   if (!pid)
93:     {
94:       tcb = this_task();
95:     }
96:   else
97:     {
98:       tcb = nxsched_get_tcb(pid);
99:     }
100: 
101:   if (tcb == NULL)
102:     {
103:       ret = -ESRCH;
104:       goto errout;
105:     }
106: 
107:   /* Don't permit changing the affinity mask of any task locked to a CPU
108:    * (i.e., an IDLE task)
109:    */
110: 
111:   flags = enter_critical_section();
112:   if ((atomic_read(&tcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED) != 0)
113:     {
114:       ret = -EINVAL;
115:       goto errout_with_csection;
116:     }
117: 
118:   /* Set the new affinity mask. */
119: 
120:   tcb->affinity = *mask;
121: 
122:   /* Is the task still executing a a CPU in its affinity mask? Will this
123:    * change cause the task to be removed from its current assigned task
124:    * list?
125:    *
126:    * First... is the task in an assigned task list?
127:    */
128: 
129:   if (tcb->task_state >= FIRST_READY_TO_RUN_STATE &&
130:       tcb->task_state <= LAST_READY_TO_RUN_STATE)
131:     {
132:       /* Yes... is the CPU associated with the assigned task in the new
133:        * affinity mask?
134:        */
135: 
136:       if ((tcb->affinity & (1 << tcb->cpu)) == 0)
137:         {
138:           /* No.. then we will need to move the task from the assigned
139:            * task list to some other ready to run list.
140:            *
141:            * nxsched_set_priority() will do just what we want... it will
142:            * remove the task from its current position in the some assigned
143:            * task list and then simply put it back in the right place.  This
144:            * works even if the task is this task.
145:            */
146: 
147:           ret = nxsched_set_priority(tcb, tcb->sched_priority);
148:         }
149:     }
150: 
151: errout_with_csection:
152:   leave_critical_section(flags);
153:   if (pid)
154:     {
155:       nxsched_put_tcb(tcb);
156:     }
157: 
158: errout:
159:   return ret;
160: }

165:  * Description:
166:  *   sched_setaffinity() sets the CPU affinity mask of the thread whose ID
167:  *   is pid to the value specified by mask.  If pid is zero, then the
168:  *   calling thread is used.  The argument cpusetsize is the length (i
169:  *   bytes) of the data pointed to by mask.  Normally this argument would
170:  *   be specified as sizeof(cpu_set_t).
171:  *
172:  *   If the thread specified by pid is not currently running on one of the
173:  *   CPUs specified in mask, then that thread is migrated to one of the
174:  *   CPUs specified in mask.
175:  *
176:  *   This function is a simply wrapper around nxsched_set_affinity() that
177:  *   sets the errno value in the event of an error.
178:  *
179:  * Input Parameters:
180:  *   pid        - The ID of thread whose affinity set will be modified.
181:  *   cpusetsize - Size of mask.  MUST be sizeofcpu_set_t().
182:  *   mask       - The location to return the thread's new affinity set.
183:  *
184:  * Returned Value:
185:  *   0 if successful.  Otherwise, ERROR (-1) is returned, and errno is

189:  *
190:  ****************************************************************************/
191:

193:                       FAR const cpu_set_t *mask)
194: {

196:   if (ret < 0)
197:     {

442:       case SCHED_RR:
443:         atomic_or(&ptcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_SCHED_RR);
444:         ptcb->timeslice = MSEC2TICK(CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL);
445:         break;

449:       case SCHED_SPORADIC:

451:         break;
452: #endif

455:   /* Return the thread information to the caller */
456: 
457:   if (thread != NULL)

461: 
462:   /* Then activate the task */

517: /****************************************************************************
518:  * Name: nxtask_setup_stackargs
519:  *
520:  * Description:
521:  *   Allocate space on the new task's stack and will copy the argv[] array
522:  *   and all strings to the task's stack where it is readily accessible to
523:  *   the task.  Data on the stack, on the other hand, is guaranteed to be
524:  *   accessible no matter what privilege mode the task runs in.
525:  *
526:  * Input Parameters:
527:  *   tcb  - Address of the new task's TCB
528:  *   name - Name of the new task
529:  *   argv - A pointer to an array of input parameters. The array should be
530:  *          terminated with a NULL argv[] value. If no parameters are
531:  *          required, argv may be NULL.
532:  *
533:  * Returned Value:
534:  *  Zero (OK) on success; a negated errno on failure.
535:  *
536:  ****************************************************************************/
537: 
538: int nxtask_setup_stackargs(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb,
539:                            FAR const char *name,
540:                            FAR char * const argv[])
541: {
542:   FAR char **stackargv;
543:   FAR char *str;
544:   size_t strtablen;
545:   size_t argvlen;
546:   size_t nbytes;
547:   int argc;
548:   int i;
549:   int ret = OK;
550: 
551:   /* Give a name to the unnamed tasks */
552: 
553:   if (!name)
554:     {
555:       name = g_noname;
556:     }
557: 
558:   /* Get the size of the task name (including the NUL terminator) */
559: 
560:   strtablen = (strlen(name) + 1u);
561: 
562:   /* Count the number of arguments and get the accumulated size of the
563:    * argument strings (including the null terminators).  The argument count
564:    * does not include the task name in that will be in argv[0].
565:    */
566: 
567:   argc = 0;
568:   if (argv != NULL)
569:     {
570:       /* A NULL argument terminates the list */
571: 
572:       while (argv[argc])
573:         {
574:           /* Add the size of this argument (with NUL terminator).
575:            * Check each time if the accumulated size exceeds the
576:            * size of the allocated stack.
577:            */
578: 
579:           strtablen += (strlen(argv[argc]) + 1u);
580:           if (strtablen >= tcb->adj_stack_size)
581:             {
582:               ret = -ENAMETOOLONG;
583:               break;
584:             }
585:           else
586:             {
587:               /* Increment the number of args.  Here is a sanity check to
588:                * prevent running away with an unterminated argv[] list.
589:                * MAX_STACK_ARGS should be sufficiently large that this never
590:                * happens in normal usage.
591:                */
592: 
593:               if (++argc > MAX_STACK_ARGS)
594:                 {
595:                   ret = -E2BIG;
596:                   break;
597:                 }
598:             }
599:         }
600:     }
601: 
602:   if (ret == OK)
603:     {
604:       /* Allocate a stack frame to hold argv[] array and the strings.  NOTE
605:        * that argc + 2 entries are needed:  The number of arguments plus the
606:        * task name plus a NULL argv[] entry to terminate the list.
607:        */
608: 
609:       argvlen   = (size_t)(argc + 2) * sizeof(FAR char *);
610:       stackargv = (FAR char **)up_stack_frame(tcb, argvlen + strtablen);
611: 
612:       if (stackargv == NULL)
613:         {
614:           ret = -ENOMEM;
615:         }
616:       else
617:         {
618:           /* Get the address of the string table that will lie immediately
619:            * after the argv[] array and mark it as a null string.
620:            */
621: 
622:           str = (FAR char *)stackargv + argvlen;
623: 
624:           /* Copy the task name.  Increment str to skip over the task name
625:            * and its NUL terminator in the string buffer.
626:            */
627: 
628:           stackargv[0] = str;
629:           nbytes       = strlen(name) + 1u;
630:           strlcpy(str, name, strtablen);
631:           str         += nbytes;
632:           strtablen   -= nbytes;
633: 
634:           /* Copy each argument */
635: 
636:           for (i = 0; i < argc; i++)
637:             {
638:               /* Save the pointer to the location in the string buffer and
639:                * copy the argument into the buffer. Increment str to skip
640:                * over the argument and its NUL terminator in the string
641:                * buffer.
642:                */
643: 
644:               stackargv[i + 1] = str;
645:               nbytes           = strlen(argv[i]) + 1u;
646:               strlcpy(str, argv[i], strtablen);
647:               str             += nbytes;
648:               strtablen       -= nbytes;
649:             }
650: 
651:           /* Put a terminator entry at the end of the argv[] array. Then
652:            * save the argv[] array pointer in the TCB where it will be
653:            * recovered later by nxtask_start().
654:            */
655: 
656:           stackargv[argc + 1] = NULL;
657: 
658:           /* Initialize argv last to avoid accessing the partial initialized
659:            * fields
660:            */
661: 
662:           nxsched_get_tls(tcb)->tl_argv = stackargv;
663:         }
664:     }
665: 
666:   return ret;
667: }

58: void nxsched_unlock(FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb)
59: {
60:   irqstate_t flags = enter_critical_section();
61:   FAR struct tcb_s *ptcb;
62: 
63:   /* In non-SMP:
64:    * If lockcount equals 0 and interrupts are not masked,
65:    * an interrupt may occur just before processing the g_pendingtasks queue,
66:    * causing the scheduler to switch to and start executing a lower-priority
67:    * task. At this moment, if there is a higher-priority task in the
68:    * g_pendingtasks queue, priority inversion will occur.
69:    */
70: 
71:   rtcb->lockcount = 0;
72: 
73:   /* Note that we no longer have pre-emption disabled. */
74: 
75:   if (!up_interrupt_context())
76:     {
77:       nxsched_critmon_preemption(rtcb, false, return_address(0));
78:       sched_note_preemption(rtcb, false);
79:     }
80: 
81:   /* Release any ready-to-run tasks that have collected in
82:    * g_pendingtasks.
83:    *
84:    * NOTE: This operation has a very high likelihood of causing
85:    * this task to be switched out!
86:    */
87: 
88: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
89:   ptcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
90:   if (ptcb && ptcb->sched_priority > rtcb->sched_priority &&
91:       nxsched_deliver_task(rtcb->cpu, rtcb->cpu, SWITCH_HIGHER))
92: #else
93:   ptcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_pendingtasks());
94:   if (ptcb && nxsched_merge_pending())
95: #endif
96:     {
97:       nxsched_switch(this_task(), rtcb);
98:     }
99: 
100: #if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0
101:   /* If (1) the task that was running supported round-robin
102:    * scheduling and (2) if its time slice has already expired, but
103:    * (3) it could not slice out because pre-emption was disabled,
104:    * then we need to swap the task out now and reassess the interval
105:    * timer for the next time slice.
106:    */
107: 
108:   if ((atomic_read(&rtcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK) ==
109:       TCB_FLAG_SCHED_RR && rtcb->timeslice == 0)
110:     {
111:       /* Yes.. that is the situation.  But one more thing.  The call
112:        * to nxsched_merge_pending() above may have actually replaced
113:        * the task at the head of the ready-to-run list.  In that
114:        * case, we need only to reset the timeslice value back to the
115:        * maximum.
116:        */
117: 
118:       if (rtcb != this_task())
119:         {
120:           rtcb->timeslice = MSEC2TICK(CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL);
121:         }
122: #  ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS
123:       else if ((atomic_or(&rtcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_PREEMPT_SCHED) &
124:                 TCB_FLAG_PREEMPT_SCHED) == 0)
125:         {
126:           nxsched_reassess_timer();
127:           atomic_and(&rtcb->flags, ~TCB_FLAG_PREEMPT_SCHED);
128:         }
129: #  endif
130:     }
131: #endif
132: 
133: #ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_SPORADIC
134: #  if CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL > 0
135:   else
136: #  endif
137:   /* If (1) the task that was running supported sporadic scheduling
138:    * and (2) if its budget slice has already expired, but (3) it
139:    * could not slice out because pre-emption was disabled, then we
140:    * need to swap the task out now and reassess the interval timer
141:    * for the next time slice.
142:    */
143: 
144:   if ((atomic_read(&rtcb->flags) & TCB_FLAG_POLICY_MASK) ==
145:       TCB_FLAG_SCHED_SPORADIC && rtcb->timeslice < 0)
146:     {
147:       /* Yes.. that is the situation.  Force the low-priority state
148:        * now
149:        */
150: 
151:       nxsched_sporadic_lowpriority(rtcb);
152: 
153: #  ifdef CONFIG_SCHED_TICKLESS
154:       /* Make sure that the call to nxsched_merge_pending() did not
155:        * change the currently active task.
156:        */
157: 
158:       if (rtcb == this_task() &&
159:           (atomic_or(&rtcb->flags, TCB_FLAG_PREEMPT_SCHED) &
160:            TCB_FLAG_PREEMPT_SCHED) == 0)
161:         {
162:           nxsched_reassess_timer();
163:           atomic_and(&rtcb->flags, ~TCB_FLAG_PREEMPT_SCHED);
164:         }
165: #  endif
166:     }
167: #endif
168: 
169:   leave_critical_section(flags);
170: }

68: #ifndef CONFIG_SMP
69: bool nxsched_add_readytorun(FAR struct tcb_s *btcb)
70: {
71:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
72:   bool ret;
73: 
74:   /* Check if pre-emption is disabled for the current running task and if
75:    * the new ready-to-run task would cause the current running task to be
76:    * pre-empted.  NOTE that IRQs disabled implies that pre-emption is
77:    * also disabled.
78:    */
79: 
80:   if (rtcb->lockcount > 0 && rtcb->sched_priority < btcb->sched_priority)
81:     {
82:       /* Yes.  Preemption would occur!  Add the new ready-to-run task to the
83:        * g_pendingtasks task list for now.
84:        */
85: 
86:       nxsched_add_prioritized(btcb, list_pendingtasks());
87:       btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_PENDING;
88:       ret = false;
89:     }
90: 
91:   /* Otherwise, add the new task to the ready-to-run task list */
92: 
93:   else if (nxsched_add_prioritized(btcb, list_readytorun()))
94:     {
95:       /* The new btcb was added at the head of the ready-to-run list.  It
96:        * is now the new active task!
97:        */
98: 
99:       DEBUGASSERT(rtcb->lockcount == 0 && !is_idle_task(btcb));
100: 
101:       btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING;
102:       btcb->flink->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
103:       up_update_task(btcb);
104:       ret = true;
105:     }
106:   else
107:     {
108:       /* The new btcb was added in the middle of the ready-to-run list */
109: 
110:       btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
111:       ret = false;
112:     }
113: 
114:   return ret;
115: }
116: 
117: #else /* !CONFIG_SMP */
118: 
119: /****************************************************************************
120:  * Name:  nxsched_switch_running
121:  *
122:  * Description:
123:  *   This function switches the head of the current CPU's assigned tasks
124:  *   list to the TCB given as parameter. The idle task is not switched out.
125:  *   If the running task can't be swapped out, the btcb is pushed to
126:  *   the ready-to-run list.
127:  *
128:  * Input Parameters:
129:  *   cpu          - Always this_cpu(). Given as argument only for
130:  *                  optimization
131:  *   switch_equal - When true, switch away a task of equal priority compared
132:  *                  to the pending one
133:  *
134:  * Returned Value:
135:  *   true if the currently active task is switched
136:  *
137:  * Assumptions:
138:  * - The caller has established a critical section
139:  * - The caller has already removed the input rtcb from whatever list it
140:  *   was in.
141:  * - The caller handles the condition that occurs if the head of the
142:  *   assigned tasks list has changed.
143:  *
144:  ****************************************************************************/
145: 
146: bool nxsched_switch_running(int cpu, bool switch_equal)
147: {
148:   FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = current_task(cpu);
149:   int sched_priority = rtcb->sched_priority;
150:   FAR struct tcb_s *btcb;
151:   bool ret = false;
152: 
153:   DEBUGASSERT(cpu == this_cpu());
154: 
155:   if (nxsched_islocked_tcb(rtcb))
156:     {
157:       return false;
158:     }
159: 
160:   if (switch_equal && sched_priority > 0)
161:     {
162:       sched_priority--;
163:     }
164: 
165:   /* If there is a task in readytorun list, which is eglible to run on this
166:    * CPU, and has higher priority than the current task,
167:    * switch the current task to that one.
168:    */
169: 
170:   for (btcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
171:        btcb && btcb->sched_priority > sched_priority;
172:        btcb = btcb->flink)
173:     {
174:       /* Check if the task found in ready-to-run list is allowed to run on
175:        * this CPU. TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED may be used to override affinity. If
176:        * the flag is set, assume that btcb->cpu is valid, and it is the only
177:        * CPU on which the btcb can run.
178:        */
179: 
180:       if (CPU_ISSET(cpu, &btcb->affinity) &&
181:           ((btcb->flags & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED) == 0 || btcb->cpu == cpu))
182:         {
183:           /* Found a task, remove it from ready-to-run list */
184: 
185:           dq_rem((FAR struct dq_entry_s *)btcb, list_readytorun());
186: 
187:           if (!is_idle_task(rtcb))
188:             {
189:               /* Put currently running task back to ready-to-run list */
190: 
191:               rtcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
192:               nxsched_add_prioritized(rtcb, list_readytorun());
193:             }
194:           else
195:             {
196:               rtcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_ASSIGNED;
197:             }
198: 
199:           per_cpu_var_smp(g_assignedtasks, cpu) = btcb;
200:           up_update_task(btcb);
201: 
202:           btcb->cpu = cpu;
203:           btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING;
204:           ret = true;
205:           break;
206:         }
207:     }
208: 
209:   return ret;
210: }
211: 
212: /****************************************************************************
213:  * Name:  nxsched_add_readytorun
214:  *
215:  * Description:
216:  *   This function adds a TCB to one of the ready to run lists. The list
217:  *   will be:
218:  *
219:  *   1. The g_readytorun list if the task is ready-to-run but not running
220:  *      and not assigned to a CPU.
221:  *   2. The g_assignedtask[cpu] list if the task is running or if has been
222:  *      assigned to a CPU.
223:  *
224:  *   If the currently active task has preemption disabled and the new TCB
225:  *   would cause this task to be pre-empted, the new task is added to the
226:  *   g_pendingtasks list instead.  The pending tasks will be made
227:  *   ready-to-run when preemption isunlocked.
228:  *
229:  * Input Parameters:
230:  *   btcb - Points to the blocked TCB that is ready-to-run
231:  *
232:  * Returned Value:
233:  *   true if the currently active task (the head of the ready-to-run list)
234:  *   has changed.
235:  *
236:  * Assumptions:
237:  * - The caller has established a critical section before calling this
238:  *   function (calling sched_lock() first is NOT a good idea -- use
239:  *   enter_critical_section()).
240:  * - The caller has already removed the input rtcb from whatever list it
241:  *   was in.
242:  * - The caller handles the condition that occurs if the head of the
243:  *   ready-to-run list has changed.
244:  *
245:  ****************************************************************************/
246: 
247: bool nxsched_add_readytorun(FAR struct tcb_s *btcb)
248: {
249:   bool doswitch = false;
250:   int target_cpu = btcb->flags & TCB_FLAG_CPU_LOCKED ? btcb->cpu :
251:     nxsched_select_cpu(btcb->affinity);
252:   FAR struct tcb_s *tcb = current_task(target_cpu);
253: 
254:   /* Add the btcb to the ready to run list, and try to run it on the target
255:    * CPU
256:    */
257: 
258:   btcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN;
259:   nxsched_add_prioritized(btcb, list_readytorun());
260: 
261:   /* In some cases, such as setaffinity, cpu need to be used. */
262: 
263:   btcb->cpu = target_cpu;
264:   if (tcb->sched_priority < btcb->sched_priority)
265:     {
266:       doswitch = nxsched_deliver_task(this_cpu(), target_cpu,
267:                                       SWITCH_HIGHER);
268:     }
269: 
270:   return doswitch;
271: }

63:    * nxsched_remove_readytorun will return true if we just

76:    * switch only if the EXCLUSIVE or of the two calls is non-zero
77:    * (i.e., one and only one the calls changes the head of the
78:    * ready-to-run list).

44: /****************************************************************************
45:  * Name:  nxsched_running_setpriority
46:  *
47:  * Description:
48:  *   This function sets the priority of a running task.  This does nothing
49:  *   if we are increasing the priority of a running task.  If we are dropping
50:  *   the priority of a running task, then this could cause then next lower
51:  *   priority task to run,
52:  *
53:  *   NOTE: Setting a task's priority to the same value has a similar effect
54:  *   to sched_yield() -- The task will be moved to after all other tasks
55:  *   with the same priority.
56:  *
57:  * Input Parameters:
58:  *   tcb - the TCB of task to reprioritize.
59:  *   sched_priority - The new task priority
60:  *
61:  * Returned Value:
62:  *   None
63:  *
64:  ****************************************************************************/
65: 
66: static inline void nxsched_running_setpriority(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb,
67:                                                int sched_priority)
68: {
69:   FAR struct tcb_s *nxttcb;
70: 
71:   /* Get the TCB of the next highest priority, ready to run task */
72: 
73: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
74:   nxttcb = (FAR struct tcb_s *)dq_peek(list_readytorun());
75: #else
76:   nxttcb = tcb->flink;
77: #endif
78: 
79:   /* A context switch will occur if the new priority of the running
80:    * task becomes less than OR EQUAL TO the next highest priority
81:    * ready to run task.
82:    */
83: 
84: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
85: 
86:   /* A context switch will occur:
87:    * CASE 1. The new priority of the running task becomes less than or
88:    * equal to the next highest priority ready to run task.
89:    * CASE 2. In SMP, the affinity of tcb has changed and no longer includes
90:    * the current cpu.
91:    */
92: 
93:   if ((nxttcb && sched_priority <= nxttcb->sched_priority) ||
94:       (tcb->affinity & (1 << tcb->cpu)) == 0)
95: #else
96:   if (nxttcb && sched_priority <= nxttcb->sched_priority)
97: #endif
98:     {
99: #ifdef CONFIG_SMP
100:       tcb->sched_priority = sched_priority;
101:       if (nxsched_deliver_task(this_cpu(), tcb->cpu, SWITCH_EQUAL))
102:         {
103:           nxsched_switch(this_task(), tcb);
104:         }
105: #else
106:       FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
107: 
108:       if (rtcb->lockcount > 0)
109:         {
110:           /* Move all tasks with the higher or the same priority from
111:            * the ready-to-run list to the pending list.
112:            * If a running task has the same priority as other tasks on
113:            * the pending list, it must be executed last.
114:            */
115: 
116:           while (sched_priority <= nxttcb->sched_priority)
117:             {
118:               bool check = nxsched_remove_readytorun(nxttcb);
119:               DEBUGASSERT(check == false);
120:               UNUSED(check);
121: 
122:               nxsched_add_prioritized(nxttcb, list_pendingtasks());
123:               nxttcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_PENDING;
124: 
125:               nxttcb = tcb->flink;
126:             }
127: 
128:           /* Change the task priority */
129: 
130:           tcb->sched_priority = sched_priority;
131:         }
132:       else
133:         {
134:           /* A context switch will occur. */
135: 
136:           if (nxsched_reprioritize_rtr(tcb, sched_priority))
137:             {
138:               nxsched_switch(this_task(), rtcb);
139:             }
140:         }
141: #endif
142:     }
143: 
144:   /* Otherwise, we can just change priority since it has no effect */
145: 
146:   else
147:     {
148:       /* Change the task priority */
149: 
150:       tcb->sched_priority = sched_priority;
151:     }
152: }

248:  *   This function sets the priority of a specified task.
249:  *
250:  *   NOTE: Setting a task's priority to the same value has a similar effect
251:  *   to sched_yield() -- The task will be moved to after all other tasks
252:  *   with the same priority.
253:  *
254:  * Input Parameters:
255:  *   tcb - the TCB of task to reprioritize.
256:  *   sched_priority - The new task priority
257:  *
258:  * Returned Value:
259:  *   On success, nxsched_set_priority() returns 0 (OK). On error, a negated
260:  *   errno value is returned.
261:  *
262:  *  EINVAL The parameter 'param' is invalid or does not make sense for the
263:  *         current scheduling policy.
264:  *  EPERM  The calling task does not have appropriate privileges.
265:  *  ESRCH  The task whose ID is pid could not be found.
266:  *
267:  ****************************************************************************/
268: 
269: int nxsched_set_priority(FAR struct tcb_s *tcb, int sched_priority)
270: {
271:   irqstate_t flags;
272:   int ret = OK;
273: 
274:   /* Verify that the requested priority is in the valid range */
275: 
276:   if (sched_priority >= SCHED_PRIORITY_MIN &&
277:       sched_priority <= SCHED_PRIORITY_MAX)
278:     {
279:       /* We need to assure that there there is no interrupt activity while
280:        * performing the following.
281:        */
282: 
283:       flags = enter_critical_section();
284: 
285:       /* There are three major cases (and two sub-cases) that must be
286:        * considered:
287:        */
288: 
289:       switch (tcb->task_state)
290:         {
291:           /* CASE 1. The task is running and a context switch may be caused
292:            * by the re-prioritization
293:            */
294: 
295:           case TSTATE_TASK_RUNNING:
296:             nxsched_running_setpriority(tcb, sched_priority);
297:             break;
298: 
299:           /* CASE 2. The task is ready-to-run (but not running) and a context
300:            * switch may be caused by the re-prioritization
301:            */
302: 
303:           case TSTATE_TASK_READYTORUN:
304:             nxsched_readytorun_setpriority(tcb, sched_priority);

308:            * Priority cannot effect the currently executing task.
309:            */
310:

313:             break;

398:  *   pthread_setup_scheduler().

400:  * Input Parameters:

402:  *   priority   - Priority of the new task
403:  *   start      - Thread startup routine
404:  *   entry      - Thread user entry point
405:  *   ttype      - Type of the new thread: task, pthread, or kernel thread
406:  *
407:  * Returned Value:
408:  *   OK on success; ERROR on failure.

410:  *   This function can only failure is it is unable to assign a new, unique

416:                                     start_t start, CODE void *entry,
417:                                     int ttype)

424:

429:

# Findings

I inspected the current AP source tree, the sibling NuttX tree used by this workspace, the generated configuration, and the project’s own historical bring-up notes. No files were modified.

The important distinction is:

> `kthread_create()` does not wait for the new worker to report that it has started. It allocates and initializes a TCB, activates it on a scheduler run queue, and returns the PID. If the call really never returns, the stall is in TCB allocation/setup, scheduler activation, a scheduler/critical-section interaction, or an SMP scheduling IPI—not in `mb_uart_worker()` itself.

The most likely AP-specific cause in the current sequence is that `bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()` enables the global SysTick before the `mb-uart0` TCB is created. That opens a first-tick/SMP scheduler race exactly between the successful mailbox-worker start and the UART worker creation.

A second important defect is that all of the new deferred worker-start functions report success once `kthread_create()` returns, even if the worker immediately exits because its CPU-affinity check fails. There is no ready handshake for `mb-uart0`, `mbox-v2`, or `mbox-diag`.

---

# 1. Actual bring-up call chain

## 1.1 NuttX invokes `board_late_initialize()` from the AppBringUp kernel thread

The standard local NuttX bring-up path is:

```text
nx_bringup()
  -> nx_create_initthread()
       -> nxthread_create("AppBringUp", ...)
  -> AppBringUp/nx_start_task()
       -> nx_start_application()
            -> board_late_initialize()
```

Relevant paths and lines:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/init/nx_bringup.c:441-455`

  `nx_create_initthread()` creates the `AppBringUp` kernel thread using:

  ```c
  nxthread_create("AppBringUp", TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_KERNEL,
                  CONFIG_BOARD_INITTHREAD_PRIORITY,
                  NULL, CONFIG_BOARD_INITTHREAD_STACKSIZE,
                  nx_start_task, NULL, environ);
  ```

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/init/nx_bringup.c:414-420`

  `nx_start_task()` calls `nx_start_application()`.

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/init/nx_bringup.c:326-334`

  `nx_start_application()` directly calls:

  ```c
  board_late_initialize();
  ```

The active project configuration confirms:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/nsh/defconfig:43`

  ```text
  CONFIG_BOARD_INITTHREAD_PRIORITY=100
  ```

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/configs/nsh/defconfig:44`

  ```text
  CONFIG_BOARD_LATE_INITIALIZE=y
  ```

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:420-435`

  The generated configuration has SMP enabled, two NuttX logical CPUs, and a 200 ms round-robin interval:

  ```text
  CONFIG_SMP=y
  CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS=2
  CONFIG_SMP_DEFAULT_CPUSET=0x3
  CONFIG_RR_INTERVAL=200
  # CONFIG_SCHED_NOPREEMPT_KERNEL is not set
  ```

The project’s `board_late_initialize()` adds another layer:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:202-228`

It creates a detached pthread:

```c
pthread_attr_setdetachstate(&attr, PTHREAD_CREATE_DETACHED);
pthread_attr_setstacksize(&attr, 4096);
pthread_attr_setinheritsched(&attr, PTHREAD_EXPLICIT_SCHED);
param.sched_priority = 100;
...
CPU_SET(0, &cpuset);
pthread_attr_setaffinity_np(&attr, sizeof(cpuset), &cpuset);
...
pthread_create(&thread, &attr, bk7258_bringup_worker, NULL);
```

The worker then enters the actual bring-up:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:164-199`

```c
static void *bk7258_bringup_worker(void *arg)
{
  int ret = bk7258_bringup();
  ...
}
```

The relevant calls are:

- `bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()` at line 56
- `bk7258_mb_uart_worker_start()` at line 65
- the stage after the mailbox worker start at line 63
- the stage after the UART worker start at line 72

So the observed interval is:

```text
bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()
  returns OK
  -> BK7258_BOOT_BRINGUP_WORKERS
  -> bk7258_mb_uart_worker_start()
       -> kthread_create("mb-uart0", 95, 2048, ...)
```

---

# 2. Local NuttX `kthread_create()` implementation

## 2.1 Public API

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/include/nuttx/kthread.h:83-107`

The API contract says that `kthread_create()`:

- creates and activates a kernel-mode task;
- returns a positive PID on success;
- returns a negative errno value on failure;
- does not promise that the worker entry point has executed before it returns.

The declaration is:

```c
int kthread_create(FAR const char *name, int priority, int stack_size,
                   main_t entry, FAR char * const argv[]);
```

The stack size is passed as an integer byte count. Therefore `2048` means a 2048-byte requested kernel-thread stack; it is not a priority or word count.

## 2.2 `kthread_create()` is a thin wrapper

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/task/task_create.c:269-298`

```c
int kthread_create(...)
{
  return kthread_create_with_stack(name, priority,
                                   NULL, stack_size, entry, argv);
}
```

`kthread_create_with_stack()` calls:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/task/task_create.c:261-266`

```c
return nxthread_create(name, TCB_FLAG_TTYPE_KERNEL, priority,
                       stack_addr, stack_size, entry, argv, NULL);
```

## 2.3 Common task creation path

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/task/task_create.c:77-128`

The sequence is:

1. Initialize spawn attributes:

   - lines 86-90

2. Allocate a TCB:

   - lines 91-99

   ```c
   tcb = kmm_zalloc(...);
   ```

3. Initialize the task:

   - line 108

   ```c
   ret = nxtask_init(tcb, name, entry, NULL, &attr, argv, envp);
   ```

4. Save the PID:

   - lines 118-119

5. Activate the task:

   - line 122

   ```c
   nxtask_activate(tcb);
   ```

6. Return the PID:

   - lines 124-125

There is no semaphore wait, child-ready wait, or worker-entry handshake in this path.

Thus, if tracing shows that execution reaches line 122 but never reaches line 124, the problem is in scheduler activation or a context switch—not in the new worker’s body.

## 2.4 Task initialization can allocate and manipulate scheduler state

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/task/task_init.c:213-306`

`nxtask_init()`:

- initializes the kernel task group;
- initializes exit/join state;
- calls `task_setup()`;
- returns only after scheduler setup has completed.

The stack is allocated in:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/task/task_init.c:101-112`

For a normal dynamically allocated kernel thread, this calls:

```c
up_create_stack(tcb, stacksize, ttype);
```

The stack-argument and scheduler setup path is then entered through:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/task/task_init.c:130-141`

The `kthread_create()` call may therefore encounter:

- kernel heap allocation;
- TCB allocation;
- stack allocation;
- PID-table locking;
- task-group initialization;
- TLS initialization;
- scheduler TCB initialization;
- scheduler-list insertion.

A resource shortage should normally return `-ENOMEM`; it should not be an intentional wait. Nevertheless, heap-lock or scheduler-lock contention is a possible location for a true stall.

---

# 3. Scheduler setup and critical-section requirements

## 3.1 Affinity is inherited during common scheduler setup

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/task/task_setup.c:216-245`

The NuttX comment explicitly states that `task_create()` and kernel-thread creation inherit the parent’s CPU affinity.

The implementation is:

```c
FAR struct tcb_s *rtcb = this_task();
tcb->affinity = rtcb->affinity;
```

Specifically:

- line 240 obtains the current task;
- line 241 copies the current task’s affinity.

This is the reason the AP tries to pin the creator before calling `kthread_create()`.

## 3.2 Scheduler initialization briefly enters a global critical section

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/task/task_setup.c:415-510`

The important parts are:

- lines 423-425: allocate a unique PID;
- lines 436-442: store priority, startup routine, and entry point;
- lines 468-477: inherit affinity;
- lines 498-500: call architecture-specific initial-state setup;
- lines 504-507: enter a critical section and insert the TCB on the inactive-task list.

The critical section is explicitly internal to NuttX:

```c
flags = enter_critical_section();
dq_addfirst((FAR dq_entry_t *)tcb, list_inactivetasks());
tcb->task_state = TSTATE_TASK_INACTIVE;
leave_critical_section(flags);
```

The caller is not expected to establish a critical section around `kthread_create()`.

## 3.3 Activation establishes another critical section and may switch

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/task/task_activate.c:64-109`

```c
irqstate_t flags = enter_critical_section();
...
nxsched_remove_blocked(tcb);
...
if (nxsched_add_readytorun(tcb))
  {
    nxsched_switch(this_task(), rtcb);
  }
leave_critical_section(flags);
```

The activation path can perform a scheduler switch before returning from `nxtask_activate()`.

This is particularly important for SMP because the task is placed on a CPU-specific scheduler path, and the current CPU may send a scheduling IPI to another CPU.

## 3.4 `nxsched_add_readytorun()` requires a critical section, but not `sched_lock()`

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_addreadytorun.c:41-66`

The local NuttX comment is explicit:

```text
The caller has established a critical section before calling this function
(calling sched_lock() first is NOT a good idea -- use enter_critical_section()).
```

The SMP implementation is:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_addreadytorun.c:247-270`

The relevant sequence is:

```c
target_cpu = ... nxsched_select_cpu(btcb->affinity);
tcb = current_task(target_cpu);
...
btcb->cpu = target_cpu;
if (tcb->sched_priority < btcb->sched_priority)
  {
    doswitch = nxsched_deliver_task(this_cpu(), target_cpu,
                                    SWITCH_HIGHER);
  }
```

Therefore:

- the target CPU is selected from the new task’s affinity;
- the TCB is added to the ready-to-run list;
- if it outranks the current task on the target CPU, NuttX may request a remote schedule;
- the caller must already be in the internal critical section;
- ordinary application code should not wrap creation with `sched_lock()` or an IRQ-disabled region.

## 3.5 Remote scheduling uses an SMP scheduling IPI

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/sched/sched.h:483-512`

If the target CPU differs from the creator CPU:

```c
per_cpu_var_smp(g_delivertasks, target_cpu) = priority;
up_send_smp_sched(target_cpu);
```

The BK7258 implementation is:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:194-203`

```c
int up_send_smp_sched(int cpu)
{
  int ret = bk7258_smp_kick(cpu, BK7258_IPI_SCHED);
  ...
}
```

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_smpcall.c:78-123`

`bk7258_smp_kick()`:

- records the pending bit;
- claims the kick;
- writes a raw mailbox kick;
- retries if the FIFO is full;
- clears the kick state on non-`EAGAIN` failure or retry timeout.

The receiving side processes the delivered scheduling request in:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_process_delivered.c:41-100`

This code assumes:

- it is called from interrupt context;
- the current CPU is not locked;
- a failed local scheduling delivery may be forwarded to another eligible CPU.

This is a plausible stall boundary if the system’s scheduling IPI path is interrupted or if one AP logical CPU is trapped in a critical section.

## 3.6 `sched_lock()` is not a protection mechanism for task creation

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/include/nuttx/sched.h:283-314`

`sched_lock()` increments the current TCB’s `lockcount`. Its documented behavior is to disable preemption, not to provide general mutual exclusion.

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_lock.c:79-115`

The implementation comment says the caller remains the only runnable task until it unlocks or blocks.

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_unlock.c:58-99`

When the lock is released, pending or higher-priority work may immediately cause a context switch.

The practical requirements here are:

1. Do not call `kthread_create()` from interrupt context.
2. Do not call it while holding `g_bk7258_driver_lock`.
3. Do not call it while holding an unrelated `sched_lock()`.
4. Do not call it with interrupts disabled.
5. Do not assume that creating a lower-priority task makes its entry point run immediately.
6. Allow NuttX’s own `enter_critical_section()`/`leave_critical_section()` around scheduler-list operations to do their work.

The current `bk7258_bringup()` caller does not visibly hold `g_bk7258_driver_lock` around the worker creation. That makes a direct caller-side recursive-lock problem less likely at this exact call site, although a global scheduler lock held by another CPU remains possible.

The active generated configuration also has:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/cmake_out/bk7258-ap_nsh/.config:435`

  ```text
  # CONFIG_SCHED_NOPREEMPT_KERNEL is not set
  ```

Therefore the new kernel workers are not automatically started with kernel-task preemption disabled in this build.

---

# 4. POSIX pthread creation and the CPU0 affinity

## 4.1 The public pthread wrapper

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/libs/libc/pthread/pthread_create.c:68-92`

`pthread_create()` is only a wrapper around `nx_pthread_create()`.

## 4.2 pthread creation applies the explicit affinity before activation

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/pthread/pthread_create.c:188-225`

The parent is obtained at:

- lines 202-203

The pthread TCB and stack are allocated at:

- lines 218-225
- lines 257-270

The scheduler TCB is initialized at:

- lines 395-409

The important SMP behavior is:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/pthread/pthread_create.c:411-423`

First, common setup inherited the parent’s affinity. Then, because the pthread attributes contain a nonzero affinity, it overrides the inherited value:

```c
if (attr->affinity != 0)
  {
    ptcb->affinity = attr->affinity;
  }
```

The pthread is activated only afterward:

- lines 425-427: join group;
- lines 455-464: return the pthread PID and activate it.

Thus, for the current code, the CPU0 affinity is placed into the TCB before `nxtask_activate()`.

## 4.3 `pthread_attr_setaffinity_np()` itself only writes the attribute

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/libs/libc/pthread/pthread_attr_setaffinity.c:54-65`

It simply does:

```c
attr->affinity = *cpuset;
```

The board ignores the return value at:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:216-220`

The local implementation returns `OK` unless a debug assertion fires, so ignoring the return is not probably the immediate hang, but it is still worth checking in a trace.

## 4.4 The mailbox code pins the current creator again

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:158-168`

`bind_worker_to_primary()` sets the current thread’s affinity to CPU0.

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1096-1107`

`bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()` first waits for the secondary scheduler and then pins the creator:

```c
ret = wait_secondary_scheduler();
...
CPU_ZERO(&cpuset);
CPU_SET(0, &cpuset);
ret = sched_setaffinity(0, sizeof(cpuset), &cpuset);
```

This ordering is intentional and should not be reversed. The project’s own notes document that sending an SMP IPI too early, during the secondary boot/exception-return window, caused a startup regression:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:694-706`

The current code waits for secondary readiness before changing affinity or creating the mailbox workers:

- `wait_secondary_scheduler()` at `bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:171-188`
- the call at `bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1090`

That is the correct general ordering.

## 4.5 `sched_setaffinity()` can itself invoke scheduler migration

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_setaffinity.c:74-159`

The implementation:

1. finds the TCB;
2. enters a critical section;
3. changes `tcb->affinity`;
4. if the task is running on a CPU no longer allowed, calls `nxsched_set_priority()` to move it;
5. leaves the critical section.

The migration path is therefore not a simple field assignment. It can enter scheduler reprioritization and SMP delivery.

In particular:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_setpriority.c:84-104`

When a running task’s affinity no longer contains its current CPU, NuttX may call:

```c
nxsched_deliver_task(this_cpu(), tcb->cpu, SWITCH_EQUAL);
```

If the board pthread really is already running on CPU0, this path should be inexpensive. If the pthread attribute was not honored, or if the logical/physical CPU mapping is not what the caller assumes, `sched_setaffinity(0, CPU0)` can become the first point where an SMP migration/scheduling IPI is generated.

---

# 5. BK7258 CPU and mailbox affinity constraints

The AP has two NuttX logical CPUs:

- logical CPU0: the primary AP CPU;
- logical CPU1: the secondary AP CPU, referred to in some project notes as physical CPU2;
- the CP is a separate processor and is not a NuttX SMP CPU.

The physical mailbox send path enforces an AP-only restriction:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mbox0.c:112-128`

```c
int cpu = up_cpu_index();

#ifdef CONFIG_SMP
if (cpu == 1 && (destination != 1 || data[1] != 0))
  {
    return -EPERM;
  }
#endif
```

Therefore an AP logical CPU1 caller cannot send ordinary physical CP descriptors. The transport deliberately routes logical requests through a CPU0-bound worker.

The timer has the same CPU0-only requirement:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_timerisr.c:63-75`

```c
if (up_cpu_index() != 0)
  {
```

# 7. Concrete likely root causes

## Root cause 1 — SysTick is enabled before `mb-uart0` is created

**Likelihood: highest.**

Current order:

```text
bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()
  -> create mbox-v2
  -> create mbox-diag
  -> bk7258_timer_start()
  -> return OK

bk7258_mb_uart_worker_start()
  -> kthread_create("mb-uart0", ...)
```

Exact locations:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1112-1125`
- same file, `:1138`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:56-72`

After line 1138, CPU0 can take SysTick interrupts while the parent is creating the UART worker. The timer ISR enters NuttX scheduler/timer code:

- `bk7258_timerisr()`: `bk7258_timerisr.c:38-60`
- scheduler timer processing: `bk7258_timerisr.c:52`

The first tick can also process pending SMP scheduling work:

```c
bk7258_smp_retry_pending();
nxsched_process_timer();
```

This is particularly dangerous on this port because the project history documents real first-tick and SMP scheduler stalls:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/external/bk_avdk_smp/README.md:382-420`
- `:448-451`
- `:665-675`

A `kthread_create()` call performed while the scheduler is being interrupted or while another core is holding the global scheduler spinlock can appear to stop in:

- `kmm_zalloc()` / `nxtask_init()`;
- the scheduler setup critical section;
- `nxtask_activate()`;
- `nxsched_add_readytorun()`;
- an SMP schedule IPI path.

This is the first experiment I recommend.

### Minimal AP-only fix

Create all three deferred workers before enabling SysTick. In practical terms:

- move `bk7258_timer_start()` out of `bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()`;
- create `mb-uart0` first;
- then start SysTick;
- then raise `mbox-v2` and `mb-uart0` to their active priorities.

Preserve the current ordering that waits for the secondary scheduler before changing affinity:

```text
wait_secondary_scheduler()
  -> pin creator CPU0
  -> create workers
  -> start timer
```

Do not move the affinity operation ahead of `wait_secondary_scheduler()`; the project history shows that doing so can send an SMP IPI during the sensitive secondary startup window.

A minimally invasive variant for the experiment is to create `mb-uart0` before the call at `bk7258_bringup.c:56`, then leave the timer start where it is. The cleaner structural fix is to make timer start a separate final step after the UART worker TCB has been created.

## Root cause 2 — “Mailbox workers started successfully” only means their TCBs were activated

**Likelihood: high as a diagnostic/logic problem; it may conceal the real failure.**

`bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()` sets:

```c
g_tx_worker_created = true;
```

at:

- `bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1119-1121`

and:

```c
g_diag_worker_created = true;
```

at:

- `:1131-1132`

It then sets `g_workers_started = true` at:

- `:1145`

None of these points prove that the corresponding worker entry function executed.

The worker may not run before the parent continues because:

- the parent bring-up pthread has priority 100;
- `mbox-v2` and `mb-uart0` initially have priority 95;
- `mbox-diag` has priority 80;
- all are on CPU0.

The normal scheduler behavior is therefore:

```text
parent priority 100 continues
worker priority 95 is runnable but does not preempt parent
kthread_create returns
```

That is normal and not itself a hang.

### Minimal AP-only fix

Add a bounded worker-ready handshake, following the already existing PWC pattern:

- worker posts a semaphore after successful `sched_setaffinity()`;
- creator waits for the post with a finite timeout;
- worker bind failure is propagated;
- do not set `g_worker_created`/`g_workers_started` until the handshake succeeds.

For `mb-uart0`, the worker-ready point should be immediately after:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:455-459`

For `mbox-v2`, it should be after:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:966-980`

Use the PWC implementation as the model:

- `bk7258_pm_pwc.c:334-347`
- `bk7258_pm_pwc.c:479-493`

Because the current timer is started before `mb-uart0` creation, a timed ready wait currently has a dependency on SysTick. If timer ordering is changed, either:

1. start SysTick after all TCBs are created and then perform the ready waits; or
2. use an atomic/non-blocking readiness flag for the pre-tick creation experiment, followed by a bounded wait after timer start.

## Root cause 3 — Affinity migration may still be incomplete or the CPU identity may be wrong

**Likelihood: medium, but important on this port.**

The board sets the pthread attribute to CPU0:

- `bk7258_bringup.c:216-220`

The NuttX pthread implementation applies that attribute before activation:

- `pthread_create.c:411-423`

That is stronger than a worker calling `sched_setaffinity()` after it starts.

However:

- the return value of `pthread_attr_setaffinity_np()` is ignored;
- the board does not log the actual affinity or `up_cpu_index()`;
- `bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()` calls `sched_setaffinity()` again;
- NuttX affinity changes can enter scheduler migration logic;
- the project history explicitly records cases where a task configured for CPU0 was still observed on the other AP logical CPU while its affinity was being changed.

The worker bind path is:

- mailbox worker: `bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:158-168`
- UART worker: `bk7258_mb_uart.c:97-107`, called at `:455`

The current `bk7258_timer_start()` check gives one useful constraint:

- if `bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()` reaches `g_workers_started = true`, then the caller observed `up_cpu_index() == 0` at `bk7258_timerisr.c:65`.

That reduces the likelihood that the parent was still physically running on CPU1 at the exact timer-start point, but it does not prove that:

- the pthread was CPU0-bound throughout;
- each newly created worker was first scheduled on CPU0;
- the affinity migration path did not trigger a problematic IPI;
- the worker later remained CPU0-bound.

### Minimal AP-only fix

Keep the current “wait secondary first, then pin creator” ordering, but add explicit verification:

- immediately on entry to `bk7258_bringup_worker()`;
- immediately before `bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()`;
- after `sched_setaffinity()` at `bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1103`;
- at the first instruction of `mb_uart_worker()`;
- immediately after its `bind_worker_to_primary()` call.

Record:

```text
up_cpu_index()
this_cpu()
sched_getaffinity(0, ...)
sched_lockcount()
```

Do not treat a worker-side `sched_setaffinity()` call as a readiness barrier. It is a state change plus possible scheduler migration, not proof that the worker has completed migration.

## Root cause 4 — Scheduler or critical-section deadlock triggered by the first tick or SMP delivery

**Likelihood: medium-high if the call truly never returns.**

The exact NuttX activation boundary is:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/task/task_activate.c:64-109`

The SMP delivery boundary is:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/sched/sched_addreadytorun.c:247-270`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/openvela/nuttx/sched/sched/sched.h:489-509`
- BK7258 kick path: `bk7258_smpcall.c:78-123`
- BK7258 scheduler IPI entry: `bk7258_smpcall.c:125-190`
- NuttX delivered-task processing: `sched_process_delivered.c:63-100`

A true no-return symptom after timer activation could result from:

- CPU0 entering the first SysTick and never completing `nxsched_process_timer()`;
- CPU1 holding the global NuttX scheduler lock while stuck in an interrupt or SMP path;
- CPU0 waiting for `g_schedlock`;
- a scheduling IPI being queued but not delivered;
- a remote scheduler callback attempting to operate while the target CPU is still locked;
- the BK7258 raw mailbox kick path failing and leaving the scheduling request pending.

The project’s own history contains evidence of first-tick stalls involving:

- atomics;
- scheduler/timer handling;
- the SMP/exception-return window;
- raw scheduling kicks.

The older observed trace described in the project README:

- `primary=26, secondary=10, detail[2]=0x0f` at `README.md:382-420`

was specifically used to identify a secondary first-tick stop. Although later revisions improved that path, the existence of this failure mode makes the timer-order experiment especially valuable.

### Minimal AP-only fix

If trace confirms the stall at the scheduler/activation boundary:

1. Keep SysTick disabled until all initial worker TCBs exist.
2. Keep the caller on CPU0 before any CPU0-only worker creation.
3. Do not use an extra `sched_lock()` around creation.
4. Audit the BK7258 `up_send_smp_sched()`/raw-kick path for pending-bit and FIFO retry completion.
5. Verify that no board driver holds `g_bk7258_driver_lock` while creating or reprioritizing a task.
6. Temporarily run an AP-only single-logical-CPU experiment (`CONFIG_SMP` disabled or `CONFIG_SMP_NCPUS=1`) only as a diagnostic. If the symptom disappears, it confirms the SMP scheduler/affinity/tick class, not an ordinary heap failure.

## Root cause 5 — Heap/TCB/stack allocation contention or exhaustion

**Likelihood: medium-low for a true hang; high for a fast negative return that is currently not being captured.**

By the time `mb-uart0` is created, the current sequence has allocated:

- the late bring-up pthread stack, 4096 bytes;
- `mbox-v2` TCB and 2048-byte stack;
- `mbox-diag` TCB and 1024-byte stack;
- then it attempts another TCB and 2048-byte stack.

The allocation begins at:

- `task_create.c:93-99`

and the stack allocation occurs through:

- `task_init.c:101-112`.

The expected result is `-ENOMEM`, not a wait. However, the code should print the negative return and allocator state immediately.

The 2048-byte size is not intrinsically invalid. The function signatures match the required NuttX `main_t` form:

```c
static int mb_uart_worker(int argc, char **argv)
```

at:

- `bk7258_mb_uart.c:449`

so a prototype mismatch is not the likely explanation.

### Minimal AP-only fix

Before changing stack size, add a trace around the call and report:

```text
ret
errno
free heap / heap watermark if available
current CPU
scheduler lock count
```

If it returns `-ENOMEM`, test 4096 bytes for `mb-uart0` only or defer another nonessential worker. Do not interpret an allocation failure as an affinity deadlock.

## Root cause 6 — Worker-entry failure is confused with `kthread_create()` failure

**Likelihood: high as an observability problem.**

`mb-uart0` can immediately return:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:455-459`

if binding fails.

`mbox-v2` can return due to:

- failed affinity at `:966-970`;
- secondary not ready at `:971-975`;
- final error return at `:977-980`.

But `bk7258_mb_uart_worker_start()` sets:

```c
g_worker_created = true;
g_worker_pid = ret;
```

at:

- `bk7258_mb_uart.c:568-570`

without knowing whether the worker has executed.

The same issue applies to `mbox-v2` and `mbox-diag`.

This can produce:

```text
worker-start function appears successful
no worker activity occurs
later transport waits forever or times out
```

It cannot, by itself, make the original `kthread_create()` call fail to return; it can make the surrounding bring-up appear stuck later.

# 8. Why priority 95 is not normally enough to make `kthread_create()` block

The caller’s priority is 100:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:23-24`
- `:214-215`

The new UART worker is created at priority 95:

- `bk7258_mb_uart.c:40`
- `:561-562`

The mailbox TX worker is also created at 95:

- `bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:37`
- `:1112-1113`

The normal SMP activation logic only requests a switch when the new TCB is higher priority than the target CPU’s current task:

- `sched_addreadytorun.c:264-268`

Since 95 is below the bring-up pthread’s 100, normal activation should not preempt the parent. Therefore:

- the worker’s lower priority can delay its first execution;
- it should not prevent `kthread_create()` from returning;
- if `kthread_create()` is genuinely stuck, the first suspects are scheduler/critical-section/tick activity or allocation, not the worker’s loop.

The later `sched_setparam()` raises the worker to 106:

- `bk7258_mb_uart.c:575-586`

That is a separate event and can cause a context switch, but it occurs only after `bk7258_mb_uart_worker_start()` has returned.

# 9. Additional lock-related issue to keep separate

The current mailbox code has comments and changes addressing recursive acquisition of the driver spinlock:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mb_uart.c:170-250`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_pm_pwc.c:303-331`
- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:906-908`

The transport invokes completion or RX callbacks while holding:

```c
g_bk7258_driver_lock
```

The UART callback explicitly avoids recursively taking that lock.

This is unlikely to explain a stall inside the `kthread_create("mb-uart0", ...)` call itself, because `mb_uart_worker_start()` is not called while visibly holding that lock. It can, however, cause the system to stop immediately after the worker is created if a timer or mailbox IRQ causes a callback path to re-enter the lock.

So the trace must distinguish:

```text
stuck in task creation
```

from:

```text
task creation returned; first timer/mailbox callback deadlocked
```

# 10. Recommended first experiment

## Experiment 1: defer SysTick until after `mb-uart0` has been created

This is the smallest AP-only sequencing experiment and most directly tests the leading hypothesis.

Current problematic boundary:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/chips/bk7258/bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1138`

Current call sequence:

- `/home/mi/vela_competition/contest/contest2026_264_VelaSightsuixingAIzhinengyanjing/board/beken/boards/bk7258/bk7258-ap/src/bk7258_bringup.c:56-72`

For the experiment:

1. Preserve `wait_secondary_scheduler()` at `bk7258_mailbox_channel.c:1090`.
2. Preserve creator pinning at `:1101-1107`.
3. Create `mbox-v2` and `mbox-diag`.
4. Create `mb-uart0`.
5. Only then call `bk7258_timer_start()`.
6. Activate/reprioritize the workers after the timer is running.

If changing the public function structure is inconvenient, the even simpler A/B experiment is to call `bk7258_mb_uart_worker_start()` before `bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()` at `bk7258_bringup.c:56-65`, while retaining the existing CPU0 affinity on the bring-up pthread. That tests whether the no-tick interval is the decisive factor.

### Expected result

- If the UART `kthread_create()` now returns reliably, the first-tick/scheduler-interleaving hypothesis is strongly confirmed.
- If it still stalls at exactly the same internal NuttX point, the next suspects are heap allocation or a scheduler-lock/remote-IPI deadlock.
- If the call returns but the UART worker does not run, the problem is worker scheduling/affinity or missing readiness instrumentation, not creation.

A second diagnostic experiment, only after the above, is to run a single-logical-CPU build. If the problem disappears with SMP disabled, it confirms the SMP scheduling/affinity/tick path. It does not identify which SMP component is defective, but it sharply separates it from heap or ordinary task setup.

# 12. How to interpret the first trace

| Last observed point | Most likely class |
|---|---|
| No marker before `bk7258_mb_uart_worker_start()` | Parent stopped before the call; stage/logging issue |
| Before `nxthread_create()` only | Caller never reached the call or output path is buffered |
| Inside `kmm_zalloc()` | Heap exhaustion/corruption or allocator lock |
| After allocation, before `nxtask_init()` returns | Group, stack, TLS, PID, or task setup |
| At `nxtask_setup_scheduler()` critical section | Scheduler global lock contention |
| `nxtask_activate()` entered but no return | Ready-list insertion, scheduler switch, or SMP scheduling IPI |
| Remote `up_send_smp_sched()` attempted but no send completion | BK7258 raw kick/FIFO/remote-IPI path |
| `kthread_create()` returned a negative value | Ordinary creation failure; inspect errno value, especially `-ENOMEM` |
| `kthread_create()` returned PID but no `mb_uart_worker` entry | Child has not been scheduled yet, or its trace path is broken |
| `mb_uart_worker` entry but bind fails | Affinity/migration/CPU-index issue |
| Worker passes bind but later system stops | Timer, mailbox IRQ, driver-lock, or transport progress problem |
| Timer ISR begins but does not return | First-tick scheduler/atomic/critical-section fault |
| `primary=37` but never `primary=38` | The stall is in UART worker start or the scheduler immediately after mailbox worker startup |

# 13. Recommended minimal fix order

1. **First experiment:** defer `bk7258_timer_start()` until after the `mb-uart0` TCB has been created.
2. **Add before/after trace markers** around the UART `kthread_create()` and inside `nxthread_create()`/`nxtask_activate()`.
3. **Add a bounded ready handshake** to `mb-uart0`; then do the same for `mbox-v2` and `mbox-diag`.
4. **Log actual CPU and affinity**, not just configured affinity.
5. **Verify `sched_lockcount()==0`, interrupt context is false, and no driver spinlock is held** before task creation.
6. **Only if still unresolved, run a one-logical-CPU AP diagnostic build** to isolate SMP.
7. **Only after the scheduler path is cleared, investigate heap size/stack size** and transport-level hangs.

The strongest current conclusion is:

> `bk7258_mailbox_workers_start()` returns after creating two lower-priority TCBs and enabling SysTick. It does not prove that either worker has executed. The immediate subsequent `mb-uart0` creation occurs during the first active AP tick window, while the scheduler and SMP delivery machinery are now live. On this BK7258 port, which has a documented history of first-tick and affinity/remote-IPI timing failures, that is the most credible reason for a perceived no-return at the UART `kthread_create()` boundary. The first AP-only test should move timer activation after the UART TCB creation, while preserving the existing secondary-scheduler wait before CPU0 affinity changes.
